candidates.notes: INT8 dynamic per-channel quantization. Author reports 85.6% token-exact vs fp32 oracle, chrF 97.3 vs oracle. Built for transformers.js + onnxruntime-web. Fast BPE tokenizer.json files (no SentencePiece wasm).
The indic->en direction: no other ONNX conversion of this direction exists on the Hub except TigreGotico's fp32-only repos and mobilebytesensei's fork.

candidates.rejected: en->indic only (no indic->en sibling), 335MB single files, parity documented 79.7% exact vs PyTorch. Superseded by hari31416 (smaller, both directions).
fp16 627MB (larger than int8); q4f16 73.4% exact-match vs fp32 oracle with lower chrF. int8 is the smallest AND most accurate quantization.

candidates.repo: ai4bharat originals / Raghavan / prajdabre rotary variants
candidates.rejected: PyTorch-only (fairseq format, custom modeling code). No ONNX, not browser-runnable.

preprocessing.source: IndicTransToolkit 1.1.1 (MIT) + indic-nlp-library 0.92 (MIT) + sacremoses en subset (LGPL) + urduhack 1.1.1 (MIT)
preprocessing.ported: scripts/indictrans2/processor.ts — full port: punc norm, ASCII digits, placeholders, Moses en tokenizer/detokenizer/punct-normalizer, per-script Indic normalizers (Dev/Bengali/Gurmukhi/Gujarati/Odia/Tamil/Telugu/Kannada/Malayalam/Urdu), UnicodeIndicTransliterator (offset-based script mapping + Tamil corrections), trivial tokenize/detokenize. Verified against the reference outputs documented in the naklitechie README (Bengali/Gujarati/Hindi postprocessing examples match exactly).
preprocessing.format: model input: '{src_flores} {tgt_flores} {text}' with language tags as dedicated vocab tokens; the decoder emits Devanagari-unified output for related scripts, postprocess transliterates back to the target script

inferenceProtocol.decoderStep0: decoder_model.onnx: input_ids, encoder_hidden_states, encoder_attention_mask -> logits + present.{i}.[decoder|encoder].[key|value] (18 layers)
inferenceProtocol.decoderStepN: decoder_with_past_model.onnx: input_ids, encoder_attention_mask, past_key_values.{i}.* -> logits + present.*
inferenceProtocol.browserReference: Hari31416/indictrans2-onnx-browser-demo (MIT) — proven working browser implementation with the same sessions, externalData option for the .onnx.data sidecars, and the transformers.js added-token workaround

proofResults.benchmark: P1 200-sentence FLORES-200 devtest sample, chrF++ vs professional human references, P2 quality bar (PASS_WITHIN_CHRF=2.0, BORDERLINE=5.0, MAX_FLAG_RATE=0.02)
proofResults.flagReview: Every flag on the two borderline directions is endsMidWord only, on sentences that end inside quotations (the model ends without a final period; references end mid-quote too). No wrongScript, no repeatLoop, no lengthRatio, no empty outputs anywhere. All six gaps are POSITIVE: the int8 distilled 200M beats the published full NLLB-200 600M numbers on every tested direction.

decision: SHIP in p5b: both bundles, MIT license, pinned commits, SHA-256 verified fetching, custom engine path in the worker (transformers.js tokenizers + direct ORT sessions + the processor port). Fallback to the full model with an honest message if the fetch fails.
